name: World's End
summary: The far edge of Hy Brasil, where the forests drove the Root: the burned ring, Kontar's corrupt Sylvan, the shrouded headland, the octonoid shore and Krrzck.

Living Server lore: the edge as the place the Root was driven to; the burned ring and the Red Summer; the clans of the edge who stayed too long; Kontar's soured springs; the headland of the unburned dead; the octonoid shore; Krrzck's shut town and the one outsider it let in; Eimear's account.
Mythic's 1.65 notes: the mantids keep a base at World's End from which their friends may cross to Allta Fearann, the untamed island of their legend (Dalniver arranges it).

story:
World's End is where the forests of Hy Brasil drove the Root. In the first age, the Sylvan say, the titan was everywhere under the isle, and the forests pushed him, root by root and age by age, along the high ground and east, until there was nowhere further east to push him, and he went down. The place he went down is the mouth of Galladoria. The land around it is World's End, the warm, sour coast at the far edge of the isle, and it remembers him: the ground is warm underfoot in winter, the springs taste of iron, and the trees are older and stranger than anywhere else on the isle.

Near the mouth there is a ring of ground the Sylvan call An Fáinne Dóite, the burned ring, where in the Red Summer of Sylvan memory the fire came up out of the ground itself and burned the forest from below. The fire-keepers of Domnann still keep a clean fire at its edge, as if to show the ground what fire is supposed to look like. Elro the Ancient stands west of it in the old grove, the keeper-tree who helped drive the titan to the edge and held when his brother Aroon rotted; no song moves him, and when he is wounded the old grove wakes around him. The ancient treants of the northern edge are his, slow and furious, older than the Sylvan's oldest songs.

There were clans of the edge. They were Sylvan who stayed at World's End after the Pushing to watch the place the Root went down, and they stayed too long. Their chieftain, Kontar, drank from the soured springs and called it strength, and his clan drank after him, and they are corrupt now, the corruptors of the middle edge with their chalico beasts about them. Kontar keeps a guard of menders who stayed with him, and they keep only him whole. His kin in Domnann scratch his name off the wardens' stone every spring, and every spring someone scratches it back. The clan's dead were never burned. They lie on the eastern headland, and their shrouds walk it, and the eldest of them, Archilus, tears into more of himself for every hand that strikes him.

The shore is the octonoid mothers'. Three of them keep the shallows and the cold pools under the cliffs, Balere the eldest, Mollunero the strongest, Zytka the youngest, who came out of the Red Summer alive and is hot to the touch; each comes up with her young, and the young go back into the sea when she does. The Sylvan say they crawled up out of the Underneath, the deep dark under the isle that the falls of Galladoria drink from. The elder octonids and the eight-armed things that climb the shore trees are their kin, and the Sylvan guides refuse to walk anyone to Mollunero's pool.

Inland, on the high ground in the middle of the edge, stands Krrzck, the mantids' town. It is shut. The mantids of the edge trade when trade is useful, through one go-between at a time, and keep their walls closed to every people of the isle; the Sylvan have never been inside. In all the generations of the isle exactly one outsider has been let in: Eimear, an outlander girl of Altan Garran who sat outside the wall until they opened it. She speaks for them now, coldly, and the mantids' stewards and citizens let her. Out on the plain around the town the botonid rencanraiders and the rencan herds graze, and the Krrzck hunt them.

Why does it matter? Because the edge is where the isle's oldest trouble went down, and where it comes up. Every company the realm sends into Galladoria walks through World's End to the mouth, past the burned ring and Kontar's clan and the headland of shrouds, and the Sylvan who guide them stop at the ring's edge and touch the clean fire and go no further.
legend: World's End is the eastern edge of Hy Brasil, levels 44-75, with the Galladoria entrance in the north-east. No realm town: Krrzck in the middle is the mantids' (Krrzck faction; Eimear, Zuraspa and the stewards are there). Camps: botonid rencanraiders and rencan (44-52) in the south, corruptors and chalico (45-56) around Kontar, giant anglers, savage bugbears, ancient treants (56-66) in the north, octonids and ochtapas on the shore (to 65). Bosses: Mollunero (75), Zytka (66) and Balere (65), the octonoid mothers (kill the mother and her brood vanishes); Kontar the Corrupt (65: kill his 8-10 bodyguards first, they heal only him); Archilus (58: below 90% every real player's hit spawns a shroud on that player, so let pets and bots do the hitting); Elro the Ancient (65: treants per real player at two health windows). Sylvan custom: touch the clean fire at the edge of the burned ring before you go down into Galladoria.

book.title: The Edge, as Eimear of Krrzck Tells It
pages: I sat outside the wall of Krrzck for a season and a half because I wanted to know what a town with no doors does all day. They let me in at the end of it. I have been inside since, and I speak for them when they want someone to, and I write this because Tieru of Aalid Feie asked me to, properly, and the Krrzck say a proper asking should be answered. They do not say how. I am answering it this way. They will not read it.

The edge is where your Sylvan pushed the old one, the titan, until he went down. You can feel it in the ground. It is warm in winter. The springs taste of iron, and the Krrzck do not drink from them, and they told me why without being asked, which they never do: the clan that stayed at the edge drank, and look at them. Kontar's people are in the middle of the edge with their beasts, and his menders keep him whole and nobody else, and their dead lie on the headland unburned. The Krrzck do not go to the headland.

Near the mouth of the hollow there is a ring of burned ground where the fire once came up out of the earth. Your fire-keepers keep a small clean fire at its edge, and the Krrzck think this is the most sensible thing the Sylvan have ever done. On the shore three mothers keep their young in the shallows, and one of them is hot from the old fire, and one of them is cold, and the oldest never lets her young out of her reach. The Krrzck hunt the shore in the off seasons. They do not hunt the mothers.

The Krrzck are not your friends. They are not your enemies. They are busy, and they think you talk too much. When your companies walk past our wall toward the mouth, the stewards stand on it and count you, the same way the Sylvan count you at Aalid Feie, and when fewer come back the stewards say a word I will not translate. It is not an unkind word. It is the word they use for the rencan herds in a bad winter. It means: the edge took its share.
